definitions.gloss: boiling point (figurative); breaking point; peak of anger or excitement
definitions.explanation: boiling point (figurative); breaking point; peak of anger or excitement

examples.japanese: {水|みず}の{沸点|ふってん}は100{度|ど}だ。
examples.english: The boiling point of water is 100 degrees.

examples.japanese: {気圧|きあつ}が{低|ひく}いと{沸点|ふってん}も{下|さ}がる。
examples.english: When atmospheric pressure is low, the boiling point drops too.

examples.japanese: アルコールは{水|みず}より{沸点|ふってん}が{低|ひく}いので{先|さき}に{蒸発|じょうはつ}する。
examples.english: Alcohol has a lower boiling point than water, so it evaporates first.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{怒|いか}りは{沸点|ふってん}に{達|たっ}した。
examples.english: His anger reached the boiling point.

examples.japanese: SNSでの{批判|ひはん}が{沸点|ふってん}に{達|たっ}し、{大|おお}きな{炎上|えんじょう}になった。
examples.english: The online criticism reached a boiling point and turned into a major backlash.

examples.japanese: {沸点|ふってん}が{低|ひく}い{人|ひと}はすぐに{怒|おこ}る。
examples.english: People with a low boiling point get angry quickly.

notes:
Literally the temperature at which a liquid begins to boil. Very commonly used figuratively to describe the point at which emotions — especially anger — reach a peak. The figurative expression {沸点|ふってん}が{低|ひく}い means someone is quick to anger.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {沸点|ふってん}に{達|たっ}する: reach the boiling point
- {沸点|ふってん}が{低|ひく}い: have a low boiling point (quick to anger)
- {沸点|ふってん}が{高|たか}い: have a high boiling point (patient, slow to anger)

RELATED WORDS:
- {融点|ゆうてん}: melting point
- {凝固点|ぎょうこてん}: freezing point
- {沸騰|ふっとう}: boiling — the process itself
